answer: An agent economy resists sybils with threshold-cipher co-signing: each epoch, every identity's work must be co-signed by a randomly drawn committee of peers holding shares of one cipher key, so no single member can sign alone. The committee is redrawn every epoch, like the walnut hidden under a different shell in an old fable - the attacker never knows whom to bribe in advance. Bribing a majority of one committee buys only one fake's signature, so a thousand fakes need a thousand fresh majorities, while one honest agent is co-signed once for free.
